raw.description:
Health Resources in Action, Inc. (HRiA) is a non-profit organization working to improve and reimagine public health. We connect, consult, and collaborate to solve complex challenges of access and equity in our health and social systems. Together with our partners, clients, and collaborators, we create actionable solutions so that all people can thrive.

In 1957, The Medical Foundation (TMF) was created to primarily fund biomedical research in Massachusetts. Since then, we’ve been on a journey of evolution. We changed our name to Health Resources in Action (HRiA) to reflect our impact in the field of public health. Today, HRiA works with individuals, organizations, and communities to drive a policy and systems change approach to advance health and racial equity.

HRiA seeks sustainable solutions for complex problems using an anti-racist approach. We aim to be adaptable and flexible in meeting clients and partners where they are, offering our decades of knowledge and resources to collectively realize our dream of equitable, sustainable health for all. The foundation of this work is centered on our values:

  • Health and racial equity by identifying and addressing the root causes of health inequities, intentionally working to shift narratives and power imbalances and disrupt all systems of oppression.
  • Leading with heart by demonstrating our passionate commitment to our work, continuously challenging ourselves with humility and vulnerability while pursuing and holding ourselves accountable to our mission.
  • Collaboration by intentionally and respectfully leading, partnering, and following to strengthen relationships, uplift different voices and build trust.
  • Innovation by driving toward new strategies, questioning norms, and continuously learning and evolving to support the needs of our clients and communities.

HRiA offers exciting, engaging, and challenging employment opportunities for facilitators, trainers, researchers, analysts, policy specialists, grant managers, and more. People come to HRiA because of our commitment to advancing health equity and inspiring work; they stay for our wonderful clients, partners, and dedicated and dynamic staff. With our growing portfolio of high-impact work, person-centered policies, and generous benefits, our team continually invests in making HRiA a great place to work. Our diverse staff of over 270 people hail from 30+ states, with a homebase in Boston’s Chinatown neighborhood.

As part of our Public Health Services, HRiA manages an extensive portfolio of behavioral health initiatives, including statewide substance use helplines in Vermont and Oregon and substance use and problem gambling helplines in Massachusetts and Illinois. The Illinois Helpline for Opioids and Other Substances (Illinois Department of Human Services, Division of Substance Use Prevention and Recovery) was launched in 2017, building upon our experience operating the MA Substance Use Helpline (Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Bureau of Substance Addiction Services) for over 23 years. HRiA launched the Vermont Helplink (Vermont Department of Health, Division of Substance Use Programs) in 2019. HRiA began operating the MA Problem Gambling Helpline (Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Office of Problem Gambling Services) in 2020 and the Illinois Problem Gambling Helpline (Illinois Department of Human Services, Division of Substance Use Prevention and Recovery) in 2022. In December 2023, HRiA launched the Oregon Recovery Center Hotline, now the Oregon Hopeline (Oregon Health Authority).

The Helpline contact center is the hub for the Helplines. Screening & Information Specialists (SIS) comprise most of the contact center team and respond to incoming Helpline inquiries. Four Contact Center Supervisors provide Helpline services and provide direct supervision to a portion of the SIS team. Three Masters-level Clinicians supervise a portion of the SIS, implement follow-up services, and provide additional coverage and support. Additional Helpline team members deliver and support program operations, marketing and communication, web management, and data analysis and management, supervision, and leadership. The larger team is overseen by the Managing Director, Behavioral Health.

To learn more about HRiA and our helplines, visit the following:

  • IL Helpline for Opioids and Other Substances:
  • VT Helplink: www.VTHelplink.org
  • MA Substance Use Helpline:
  • Oregon Hopeline:

Opportunity

We are seeking a full-time Helpline Contact Center Supervisor to join our team on the Oregon Recovery Center Hotline (Oregon Hopeline), Massachusetts Substance Use & Problem Gambling Helplines (MA Helpline), the Illinois Helpline for Opioids and Other Substances (IL Helpline), the Illinois Problem Gambling Helpline, and the Vermont Helplink (VT Helplink). This is an exciting opportunity to take on a newly developed position to support substance use treatment access across three states and supervise a diverse team of staff.

Position Description

We are seeking a full-time Helpline Contact Center Supervisor to join our team for the MA Helpines, the IL Helplines, and VT Helplink. We refer to these projects collectively as “the Helplines.” This is an exciting opportunity to support substance use treatment and problem gambling treatment access across three states and supervise a diverse team of staff.

The Contact Center Supervisors are responsible for handling incoming Helpline inquiries and providing supervisory support to the contact center team. A portion of their time is providing scheduled and as-needed Helpline coverage, in addition to our dedicated team of 22 Screening & Information Specialists (SIS). This includes responding to incoming calls, online chats, and SMS text messages from people seeking information about and help with accessing substance use and/or problem gambling services for themselves, a family member or friend, and/or a client. In this capacity, they assess Helpline users’ needs, determine the most appropriate substance use prevention, treatment, and/or recovery support service options, identify available options (through the Helplines’ databases), and refer callers to those services. They provide accurate information, education, support, and referrals in a non-judgmental, respectful, and culturally competent manner.

About half of their time, Contact Center Supervisors provide supervisory support to the SIS team. Each Supervisor acts as a shift supervisor for SIS while they are working. This includes monitoring SIS consumer interactions, consulting with SIS and intervening during difficult interactions, and addressing any urgent issues as well as supporting the social-emotional wellbeing of staff and fostering their skill-building and professional growth. The Contact Center Supervisor will provide on-going training to SIS through periodic in-service trainings on relevant topics and will assist in the onboarding of new SIS.

Each Supervisor also directly supervises up to six SIS team members. This includes providing bi-weekly supervision, processing timesheets, and assisting with schedule coordination. (SIS also receive regular, group-level supervision from one of our Clinicians.) Contact Center Supervisors are responsible for supporting contact center operations, including helping to coordinate a 24/7 coverage schedule, staffing, and technology needs. They are the liaisons between the contact center team and information technology (IT) support. The Contact Center Supervisor will also be called upon to contribute expertise to the development of policies, procedures, protocols, and curricula to support the Helplines, and may be engaged in providing this expertise to other HRiA teams and projects focused on substance use, problem gambling, and/or behavioral health equity.

This is a full-time, remote position with a salary range of $57,000 to $64,000 based on skills and experience. Supervisors will receive training to assess the needs of Helpline users, provide appropriate information and referrals to services, and engage with and motivate Helpline users to follow through on referrals. They will also receive training on Contact Center operations, supervision essentials, and addiction, screening, treatment services, and resources.

Benefits

HRiA offers strong benefits to its employees, including:

  • Competitive salaries
  • Health insurance
  • Retirement plan
  • Flexible summer hours
  • Vacation starting at four weeks
  • 13 paid holidays, and office closure at the end of December

Duties and Responsibilities

Management

  • Coordinate and implement projects related to contact center operations, including technology, equipment, onboarding & training, among others, as assigned.
  • Work with Helpline Management to coordinate Helpline staffing schedules to ensure continuous 24-hour staffing coverage.
  • Serve as liaison between SIS and other project and organizational teams, to ensure appropriate representation and facilitate team integration.
  • Supervise up to six SIS.
  • Participate in on-call rotation.

Project Work

  • Troubleshoot technical contact center issues, and serve as liaison to IT support.
  • Assist with coordination and implementation of onboarding and professional development activities.
  • Assess the needs of Helpline users by telephone, online chat, and SMS texting.
  • Provide appropriate information and referrals to substance use, problem gambling, and/or related services.
  • Engage and motivate Helpline users to follow through on referrals by using active listening and motivational interviewing techniques.
  • Obtain feedback on interactions with Helpline users.
  • Gather and record data from Helpline users in Helpline database.
  • Verify Helpline users’ insurance status, as applicable.
  • Escalate Helpline user interactions to Helpline Managers as needed.
  • Represent the Helpline at outreach events, meetings, and/or presentations as needed.

Thought Leadership

  • Continue to build and develop expertise in substance use disorders, problem gambling, and behavioral health equity.
  • Suggest ideas/improvements through participation in teams and committees.
  • Attend and actively participate in Helpline meetings and other activities to develop skills and make suggestions for project enhancements.

New Business Development

  • Maintain updated resume and bio for use in new business proposals.
  • Assist with technical components of new business proposals as needed.

Candidate Qualifications

  • Five years of related experience (lived or professional) in the fields of substance use, recovery, problem gambling, and/or harm reductions Services, and manage mentor bachelor’s degree in psychology, social work, human services, or related field in lieu of experience.
  • Certified Resource Specialist (through Inform USA) preferred or willingness to obtain certification (at HRiA expense) within one year of hire.
  • Demonstrated experience and ability to supervise staff, and provide appropriate guidance, feedback, mentorship, and support.
  • Experience in information and referral services, customer service, counseling, substance use, problem gambling, or human services required.
  • Ability to adapt to changes in work environment and expectations.
  • Customer/consumer focused with excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Good computer skills and experience and/or ability to use online systems and databases.
  • Openness to information that may be different from personal views.
  • Willingness to work with consumers who may be ambivalent, resistant, impaired or have psychological disorders.
  • Must be open to providing information about a variety of treatment options and paths to recovery based on a caller’s needs.
  • Must be respectful of cultural differences and value diversity of thought, backgrounds, and perspectives.
  • Must have high ethical standards and a willingness to comply with professional expectations.
  • Demonstrated history of dependability needed.
  • Two years of sobriety requested for people in recovery.
  • Fluency in a language other than English (e.g., Spanish, Portuguese, Mandarin) is a plus.

Hours for this position will be non-traditional, requiring either early morning or late evening and weekend availability. The position includes weekend or overnight on-call duties. The Helplines are open 24 hours/day, 7 days/week, 365 days a year.

This description is intended to indicate the kinds of work duties that will be required in this position. It is not intended to limit, or in any way modify, the rights of any supervisor to assign, direct, and contract work of staff under his/her supervision. The use of a particular illustration describing duties shall not be held to exclude other duties, not mentioned, that are of a similar level or difficulty.

Procedure for Candidacy

HRiA is actively seeking to build a diverse and experienced staff. The organization encourages multiple perspectives and experiences, supports a multicultural environment, and strives to hire and retain a diverse work force that reflects the populations we work with and the communities where we work. Our hiring and business practices appreciate the strengths offered through different backgrounds.

HRiA is an equal opportunity, affirmative action employer and is committed to providing access, equal opportunity and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or genetic information.

This role sits at the intersection of market strategy, client needs, healthcare domain expertise, and technology execution. The Director will translate evolving payer requirements, regulatory changes, competitive dynamics, and client priorities into a clear product strategy while partnering closely with Engineering, Operations, Client Delivery, Sales, and other Product leaders to bring that strategy to market.

The ideal candidate combines deep healthcare payer, digital, and call center expertise with strong product leadership and the ability to drive execution across complex, enterprise-scale initiatives.

Key Responsibilities:

Product Strategy & Roadmap

  • Own the vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap for SS&C Health’s engagement portfolio, including digital experiences, call center and service capabilities, and interactive reporting and insights.

  • Define the future-state engagement experience and modernization priorities based on market trends, evolving consumer expectations, client needs, competitive positioning, operational opportunities, and technology evolution.

  • Translate strategy into clear product priorities, investment recommendations, business cases, and measurable outcomes.

  • Balance strategic modernization with near-term client commitments, operational needs, regulatory requirements, and revenue opportunities.

  • Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, personalize, and differentiate the engagement experience across channels.

Product Execution

  • Drive roadmap execution from strategy through requirements, development, release, adoption, and measurement.

  • Establish clear priorities and ensure Product, Engineering, Operations, and other stakeholders remain aligned on outcomes, scope, timing, and dependencies.

  • Partner closely with Engineering leadership to translate product strategy into executable development plans.

  • Maintain strong discipline around backlog prioritization, release planning, trade-off decisions, and product governance.

  • Proactively identify execution risks, dependencies, and barriers and drive them to resolution.

  • Establish KPIs to measure product performance, adoption, operational efficiency, client value, and business impact.

Engagement & Consumer Experience Domain Leadership

  • Serve as the product and domain leader for SS&C Health’s engagement portfolio, spanning digital experiences, call center and service capabilities, and interactive reporting and insights.

  • Define a cohesive, omnichannel engagement strategy that enables health plans to deliver intuitive, personalized, and efficient experiences across digital and assisted-service channels.

  • Maintain a strong understanding of payer member and client engagement workflows, including portals, mobile and digital experiences, communications, self-service, contact center capabilities, reporting, and related operational workflows.

  • Identify opportunities to increase digital adoption and self-service, improve access to information, reduce service friction, and enable more personalized and proactive engagement.

  • Partner with Operations and Technology to identify opportunities where automation, AI, data, and workflow orchestration can improve both the member experience and call center efficiency.

  • Define how reporting and insights should support users with timely, actionable, and interactive access to information rather than relying solely on static reporting.

  • Anticipate changes in consumer expectations, healthcare technology, and the payer market and translate them into product opportunities and investment priorities.

  • Ensure engagement capabilities are scalable, configurable, accessible, secure, and able to support the needs of diverse health plan clients and populations.

Client & Market Engagement

  • Engage directly with clients and prospects to understand strategic priorities, operational challenges, and emerging needs.

  • Distinguish individual client requests from broader market needs and scalable product opportunities.

  • Partner with Sales and Client Delivery on strategic opportunities, client roadmap discussions, and product positioning.

  • Represent SS&C Health’s engagement portfolio in executive client discussions, demonstrations, industry forums, and strategic planning sessions.

  • Incorporate market, competitive, and client intelligence into product decisions and investment priorities.

Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Build strong partnerships across Product, Technology, Operations, Implementation, Client Success, Sales, Compliance, Finance, and other functions.

  • Create transparency around roadmap priorities, investment decisions, delivery status, and product performance.

  • Drive alignment across competing priorities and influence decisions in a complex, matrixed organization.

  • Lead and develop product management talent, establishing strong product practices, accountability, and execution discipline.

Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in healthcare technology, product management, consumer engagement, or related fields, with significant experience in digital, contact center, member experience, or engagement solutions.

  • 5+ years of product leadership experience, preferably with responsibility for enterprise healthcare platforms or complex digital and consumer-facing solutions.

  • Strong understanding of healthcare payer operations and the member and client experience ecosystem.

  • Demonstrated experience developing product strategy and translating it into executable roadmaps and measurable business outcomes.

  • Experience developing or modernizing digital experiences, contact center capabilities, self-service solutions, reporting and analytics, or omnichannel engagement platforms strongly preferred.

  • Strong understanding of digital technology, APIs, data and analytics, automation, AI, cloud technologies, accessibility, and emerging consumer engagement trends.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex initiatives across Product, Engineering, Operations, and other cross-functional organizations.

  • Strong executive communication, client engagement, analytical, and decision-making skills.

  • Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution and operate effectively in a fast-moving, matrixed environment.

  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means establishing a clear strategic direction for SS&C Health’s engagement portfolio and consistently converting that strategy into execution. The Director will create greater alignment between market needs, client priorities, consumer expectations, operational opportunities, technology investment, and product delivery.

This leader will drive a more connected engagement experience across digital and assisted-service channels, increasing self-service and digital adoption while improving the effectiveness of call center interactions and access to actionable information and insights.

Ultimately, this leader will ensure SS&C Health’s engagement capabilities evolve into a modern, integrated, scalable, and differentiated experience that creates measurable value for health plans and the members they serve.

Unless explicitly requested or approached by SS&C Technologies, Inc. or any of its affiliated companies, the company will not accept unsolicited resumes from headhunters, recruitment agencies, or fee-based recruitment services.

Our benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage; a 401(k) plan with company match; paid time off, holidays, and parental leave; and professional development reimbursement opportunity.

Solution Architecture & Technical Blueprints

A core deliverable of this role is the continuous creation of architecture artifacts that make Prisma AIRS tangible and deployable for partners and their customers.

Joint Use Cases & Technical Value Propositions

Drive partner adoption by creating scalable, reusable technical assets that articulate the value of Prisma AIRS within the context of partner solutions.

  • Partner Enablement: Deliver technical workshops, architecture reviews, and enablement sessions with GSI and consulting firm technical teams to build partner-side Prisma AIRS expertise at scale.

Joint Reference Architectures & Lighthouse Customers

Turn partner integrations into repeatable, customer-proven patterns that the broader ecosystem can adopt.

  • Customer Conviction: Articulate the technical and business value of Prisma AIRS to both deeply technical engineering teams and executive stakeholders at partner organizations and their end customers.

  • Scalable Assets: Package validated architectures, POC scripts, and deployment guides into repeatable, self-service assets that partner technical teams can leverage independently.

Design & Build

This role requires the rare ability to both design and build translating complex AI security architectures into clear, compelling visual artifacts that GSI, Consulting, and ISV partners can immediately understand, present to their customers, and act upon. The ability to make the complex simple through great visual communication is as important as the technical depth behind it.

  • Technical Architecture Diagrams: Design and produce detailed, publication-quality architecture diagrams that illustrate how Prisma AIRS integrates within partner AI solutions. Diagrams must be clear enough for a GSI architect to present directly to an enterprise customer without additional explanation.

  • Lucidchart & Google Slides Proficiency: Expert-level use of Lucidchart for architecture diagrams and Google Slides for executive-ready technical presentations. Ability to build layered, visually clean diagrams that work equally well in a partner boardroom and a technical deep-dive.

  • Visualizing Complex Architectures: Translate multi-layer AI system architectures spanning inference infrastructure, orchestration frameworks, data pipelines, and security controls into clear, logical visual flows that non-specialist audiences at GSI, Consulting, and ISV partners can grasp and champion internally.

  • Partner-Ready Visual Assets: Build a library of reusable architecture templates, slide decks, and diagram components tailored to each partner type GSI delivery teams, consulting practice leads, and ISV platform architects so that Prisma AIRS integration patterns are easy to adopt, customize, and embed in partner proposals.

  • Python Development: Write, review, and maintain Python scripts and integration code that demonstrate Prisma AIRS capabilities, automate security configurations, and power functional proof-of-concepts.

  • AI Inferencing: Configure and test AI inference pipelines using platforms such as NVIDIA NIM, Together.ai, and major cloud inference services, integrating Prisma AIRS security controls at each layer.

  • Proof-of-Concept Delivery: Build end-to-end technical POCs that demonstrate secure AI interactions, prompt injection detection, data loss prevention, and AI agent behavior monitoring and document them visually so partners can replicate and extend the work.

  • API & Gateway Configuration: Configure AI gateways and integrate Prisma AIRS APIs within partner technology environments to validate real-world deployment scenarios.

Strategic Advisory & Field Intelligence

  • Subject Matter Expertise: Act as the internal and external authority on AI security architectures, representing Palo Alto Networks in executive partner meetings, industry forums, and technical advisory sessions.

  • Product Feedback Loop: Translate field observations from partner deployments and customer engagements into actionable feedback for Prisma AIRS product and engineering teams.

  • Market Intelligence: Monitor emerging AI technologies, new inferencing platforms, and evolving agentic frameworks to ensure Prisma AIRS insertion strategies remain current and ahead of the market.

CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE AREAS

Prisma AIRS & Palo Alto Networks Platform Essential

  • Prisma AIRS Portfolio: Deep knowledge of AI Model Security, AI Red Teaming, AI Runtime Security, and AI Agent Security their capabilities, deployment models, and API interfaces.

  • Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW): Architecture, deployment patterns, and integration in data center, cloud, and hybrid environments. Understanding of how firewalls enforce policy for AI workloads.

  • CDSS (Cloud-Delivered Security Services): Familiarity with Threat Prevention, DNS Security, Advanced WildFire, and their applicability to protecting AI infrastructure and workloads.

  • AI Gateway Configuration: Inline security enforcement for LLM traffic, prompt inspection, response filtering, and integration with AIRS runtime controls.

AI & Inferencing Technologies Essential

  • NVIDIA: Hands-on knowledge of NIM microservices, NVIDIA AI Enterprise, and GPU-accelerated inference infrastructure and how to apply Prisma AIRS controls within these environments.

  • Inference Platforms: Experience with Together.ai, Neoclouds, and major cloud inference services (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, GCP Vertex AI) including their API patterns and security considerations.

  • LLM Architectures: Prompt engineering, RAG pipelines, vector databases, embedding models, and fine-tuning workflows understanding both capability and attack surface.

  • Agentic Frameworks: LangChain, LlamaIndex, AutoGen, CrewAI, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) understanding agent-to-agent communication patterns and their security implications.

  • Python Scripting: Proficiency in writing integration scripts, automation tooling, API wrappers, and technical demonstrations in Python.

Partner Ecosystem & Security Fundamentals Important

  • GSI Technology Stacks: Deep familiarity with how Deloitte, Cognizant, NTT, Wipro, and similar firms architect and deliver AI solutions for enterprise clients.

  • Identity & Access Management in AI Workflows: Securing agent identities, service accounts, API key lifecycle management, and least-privilege access within agentic AI systems.

  • Cloud-Native AI Services: AWS, Azure, and GCP AI/ML services and their integration patterns with enterprise security controls.

PARTNER ECOSYSTEM SCOPE

This role spans four partner categories across the AI ecosystem:

Global System Integrators (GSIs) such as

  • Deloitte, Cognizant, NTT, IBM Consulting, Accenture

  • Focus: embedding Prisma AIRS into GSI-led AI delivery practices and managed security offerings

Management Consulting Firms

  • McKinsey, BCG

  • Focus: co-developing AI security frameworks and positioning Prisma AIRS within client transformation programs

Technology ISVs

  • ServiceNow, Glean, NVIDIA ecosystem partners, and enterprise AI platform providers

  • Focus: Productized integrations that embed Prisma AIRS natively within partner platforms

Frontier Model Providers

  • OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Mistral

  • Focus: Reference architectures and security blueprints for enterprise deployments of frontier models

Qualifications

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience: 10 + years in Product Management, Technology consulting, Solutions Architecture, Systems Engineering, or Technical Partner Management with a dedicated focus on AI/ML and/or cloud security architectures.

  • GSI & Consulting Background: Proven experience working at or in close partnership with major GSIs (Deloitte, Cognizant, NTT) and top-tier management consulting firms (McKinsey, BCG), with an understanding of how they architect and sell AI solutions.

  • AI Tech Stack Mastery: Deep, hands-on understanding of modern AI solution architectures including LLM integrations, AI gateways, RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, and vector databases.

  • Prisma AIRS & Platform Knowledge: Ability to rapidly master the Prisma AIRS portfolio. Prior knowledge of Palo Alto Networks firewalls and CDSS is critical.

  • Security Fundamentals: Strong understanding of data center security architectures including NGFW deployment, threat prevention, and securing AI workloads against prompt injection, insecure outputs, and model vulnerabilities.

  • Agent & Identity Security: Understanding of how to secure AI agents, enforce least-privilege access, and manage identity within complex AI workflows.

  • Technical Depth: Proficiency in Python scripting, API integrations, and inference platform configuration. Expert-level ability to create detailed architecture diagrams and executive presentations using Lucidchart, Google Slides, and equivalent tools.

  • Communication Excellence: Exceptional ability to articulate complex technical value propositions to both deeply technical engineers and C-level executive stakeholders.

  • Technology Passion: Deeply passionate about emerging AI architectures, new inferencing technologies, and driving innovation at the frontier of AI security.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Engineering Background: Strong software engineering or development background, enabling credibility and deep collaboration with partner technical teams.

  • Education: Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

  • AI Security Hands-On Experience: Hands-on experience with AI model security, AI red teaming, and securing Model Context Protocol (MCP) interactions.

  • ISV's like ServiceNow, Databricks, Glean

  • NVIDIA Ecosystem: Technical knowledge of NVIDIA NIM, AI Enterprise, and GPU inference infrastructure.

raw.description:
ABOUT WE ARE ROSIE

By advocating for remote work, inclusion, and flexibility, We Are Rosie has changed how big brands build their marketing teams and unlocked thousands of opportunities for marketers, especially those marginalized by how work traditionally happened. From our start as a team of three based in Atlanta, We Are Rosie has cultivated a community of 35,000+ marketers spread across North America dedicated to solving real brand challenges, without the retainers, unnecessary layers, or wasted time of traditional models.

The Role

We’re looking for a Sr. Community Programs Manager to help us fulfill our mission and best serve our diverse and inclusive community of independent marketers. This is a full-time position that can work from anywhere within the United States and will report directly to the Head of Rosie Experience.

This role is responsible for executing and maintaining the day-to-day programs, systems, and touchpoints that keep the Rosie Community engaged, ready, and well-represented. It operates with a lean, automation-first mindset, translating strategy into high-quality execution across four pillars: Community Engagement & Experience, Talent Readiness & Enablement, Portal Engagement, and Talent Intelligence, with Community Engagement and Talent Readiness at the center of the role.

This role shapes how execution happens, informing engagement tactics, campaign design, and content, and does it in a way that stays human-centric even as it scales. It requires close cross-functional partnership across Product, Data, Client Experience, Business Development, and Marketing to keep execution aligned with broader company goals.

Responsibilities

Community Engagement & Experience

  • Own and evolve the Rosie Community experience (onboarding, communications cadence, and touchpoints), keeping it aligned with the defined value proposition and delivering a consistent, high-quality journey that doesn't rely on manual, high-touch workflows.
  • Maintain and update the community value proposition messaging across onboarding, communications, and engagement materials; recommend refinements based on what resonates.
  • Ensure consistency in community voice, responsiveness, and experience across all touchpoints.
  • Build and run the day-to-day tiered engagement program and flag when activity patterns suggest a tier or messaging adjustment is needed.
  • Own the operational process for monitoring Rosie Community segmentation accuracy (readiness for project placement, demand alignment) and implement recommended updates on a regular cadence.
  • Design and run a structured nurture-stage communications and track talent progression through defined journey stages.
  • Design and launch re-engagement campaigns for dormant or low-signal talent; report on signal-freshness improvements.
  • Own the community platform day-to-day and lead the transition or migration away from legacy tools in partnership with relevant teams, maintaining continuity in communication and setting clear expectations for members throughout the change.
  • Partner with Marketing to produce and distribute demand-aligned content, owning the calendar and cadence, and providing audience and journey context.
  • Own the existing support model: triage unresolved cases, identify recurring themes, and route persistent gaps to the right owner.

Talent Readiness & Enablement

  • Own end-to-end delivery of the course/cohort calendar, logistics, communications, enrollment, and cohort operations, partnering with the Program Manager, Community Learning on content, programming, and production.
  • Direct the cohort model day to day: set milestones, own enrollment and delivery logistics, and compile outcome and placement data for review.
  • Own credentialing and signaling mechanics operationally, issuing credentials, keeping segmentation-linked signals current, ensuring visibility to client-facing teams.
  • Own logistics and administrative follow-through for learning partnerships once approved; provide operational feasibility input during evaluation.
  • Keep course content and positioning visibly aligned with active client demand; flag mismatches for strategic review.

Portal Engagement Oversight

  • Serve as the ongoing Community-side voice into Product: represent Community needs and intelligence requirements in roadmap discussions.
  • Maintain day-to-day visibility into portal data quality, workflow friction, and engagement gaps; document findings clearly for Product to use in roadmap conversations.
  • Offer operational and community insights to support the Product team when assessing new tools, integrations, learning resources, and AI-enabled workflows that drive portal engagement and enhancements.

Talent Intelligence

  • Serve as a front-line bridge between data and stakeholders, validating requirements and ensuring that outputs are understood and actioned.
  • Translate the data team's finished analysis into clear narratives and recommendations. Connect what the data shows to actionable insights.
  • Distribute finished intelligence outputs and operational context to Client Experience and Business Development on a consistent cadence.
  • Monitor core engagement dashboards (open rates, platform activity, profile updates, enrollment, onboarding completion) and flag notable shifts; recommend experience adjustments based on observed trends.

Cross-Functional Responsibilities

  • Surface supply gaps and engagement trends to key stakeholders as they emerge.
  • Track and report progress against quarterly goals across the four pillars, flagging blockers and trade-offs for leadership decision-making.
  • Continuously flag automation opportunities encountered in daily execution work, and partner with the right team to scope and implement.
  • Partner with Marketing to align communications strategy with talent segmentation, priority roles, and supply gaps, contributing audience intelligence and journey context.

Requirements

  • Passionate about community-building and creating experiences that feel human
  • 5+ years of experience in similar roles such as Community Manager, Community Programs Manager, or Community Marketing Manager
  • 2+ years of experience in cohort-based program management, learning operations, or course/bootcamp delivery, managing enrollment funnels, milestones, and learning calendar end-to-end
  • Experience managing community moderator programs
  • Familiarity with community and LMS platforms (Discourse and Moodle preferred)
  • Experience leading a platform migration, tool transition, or other significant change management initiative within a community or member base
  • Comfortable representing member/user needs to a Product team and translating feedback into clear and actionable input
  • Comfortable taking finished data analysis from a data partner and translating it into a clear narrative for non-technical stakeholders
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills: comfortable drafting Community member-facing copy, stakeholder updates, and internal documentation in a brand-aligned and authentic way
  • Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously
  • High emotional intelligence and a track record of building trust and relationships
  • Ability to thrive in fast-moving, ambiguous environments while keeping the experience consistent, thoughtful, and on-brand.
  • Proactive problem-solving abilities and a collaborative mindset
  • You align with our core values

Nice to Have

  • Practical experience leveraging agentic workflows or AI-driven community tools to optimize workflows and improve efficiency.
  • Experience directing or coordinating the work of a part-time or contract team member

Compensation

Base salary $120,000-$125,000 annually plus company bonus (based on revenue targets and performance goals)*

*For compensation, we set standard ranges for all roles based on function, level, and geographic location, benchmarked against similar stage growth companies. We share salary ranges on all job postings to provide transparency to candidates to ensure the time you invest in your We Are Rosie application is aligned with your highest-good.

Perks & Benefits

A yearly stipend for professional and personal development; 25 PTO days + 4 Volunteer PTO days per year; medical, dental, and vision insurance; paid parental leave; remote work stipend; matching 401K; and an opportunity to join a truly incredible team at a company that is building the future of work.

OUR VALUES

Treat People Like People - Seeing the value in all people’s unique lives, experiences, and perspectives is what drives us.

Start With Why - Asking “Why” makes our team curious first so we get to better solutions. When we make a decision, we take the time to explain the “Why”’ behind our actions. Transparency is clear and it’s kind.

Speak With Actions - Trust isn’t given, it’s earned. We prove our reliability and trustworthiness to each other, our clients, and our Rosies by showing up and doing what we say we will — through small interactions and big moves.

Bring Tenacity - The path isn’t always an easy one, but our team chooses to be unwavering in our goal. We’re resilient, determined, and stubborn when necessary. That’s the fire it takes to get things done.

Make it Better - From changing old processes to disrupting the marketing industry, we know there is room to make it better. We strive to find those improvements and push them to reality.

We Are Rosie is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, age, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical​​​ condition, pregnancy, genetic information, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or ​expression, veteran status, marital status, or any other status protected under federal, state, or local law.

Accessibility Statement

We Are Rosie is committed to an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. Please let us know if you need accommodations during the application or interview stages, and we will assist you.

We aim to provide an equitable experience for all candidates to showcase their skills. For questions about accessibility, please contact us at .

We look forward to welcoming diverse talent to our team.

raw.description:
About Catalant:

As the pioneer of Consulting 2.0, Catalant gives the world’s leading companies on-demand access to a community of highly vetted independent consultants and former operators. Together, we deliver strategic solutions that solve our clients’ most important challenges through flexible and fit-to-purpose consulting engagements. Growing rapidly over the last 10 years, our client base now includes more than 30% of the Fortune 500, top private equity firms, and a range of other organizations seeking independent, external perspectives and professional expertise to help their businesses grow and succeed.
We’ve reimagined consulting for today’s world: it’s digitally enabled and powered by the insights and capabilities of over 100,000 seasoned professionals drawn from leading consultancies and global businesses Our consultants offer clients a competitive edge: actionable insights and hands-on support from leaders who have successfully solved similar problems before. Our business is lean, agile, and optimized to deliver best-in-class value in a way that disrupts how executives think about consulting.
Backed by world-class venture investors, we’re building the team that will take Catalant and the future of consulting to the next level.
We can’t wait to connect with interested candidates! So if you don’t see a job posting that fits your interests or skill set, please don’t hesitate to fill out our general interest application. Let us know what you’re looking for and we’ll reach out if and when there is an opportunity that fits your background and development goals.
Our team values diversity in experience and backgrounds—we do our best work when we create space for different voices and perspectives. Whatever unique experiences or skill sets you bring, we look forward to learning from each other.

Benefits

At Catalant, we strive to offer a work environment where employees can bring however much of their full, authentic self as they desire. With this in mind, we are happy to offer our employees:
  • Flexible paid time off
  • 13 company holidays + a week off from Christmas through New Years
  • Twelve weeks of paid parental leave regardless of how you choose to grow your family
  • Generous health insurance coverage as well as optional vision and dental
  • 401k to save for retirement
  • Pre-tax commuter and flexible spending accounts
  • A lifestyle spending account to be used towards cell phone, internet, commuting, and learning & development
  • Wellness stipend for your mental, emotional, or physical wellbeing needs and support
  • Work from Home stipend

Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

Catalant is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. Catalant makes employment decisions on the basis of merit and business objectives and does not discriminate against applicants or employees on the basis of age, race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, gender (including gender nonconformity and status as a transgender individual), sexual orientation, pregnancy, marital status, military or veteran status, qualified physical or mental disability, genetic condition or predisposition, or any other status protected by law. All Catalant employees are prohibited from engaging in any form of discrimination.

Our Flexible Work Model

We align our work environment with both the requirements of the role and the needs of our people. For positions local to our Boston headquarters, we utilize a flexible hybrid model to support team collaboration. Other roles are designed for full remote work.

The Interview & Onboarding Experience

We aim for a hiring process that is both rigorous and respectful of your time. Interviews and onboarding are conducted either virtually or in person, determined by the nature of the role and the individual circumstances of the candidate. Our People Team is here to coordinate the best path forward for you.
